chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic/dialogue frame and institutional-pastoral instruction aimed at catechumens vs. sinners. Even where Light/fire imagery appears (¶5), it is embedded in a catechetical comparison of ecclesial categories (catechumens/sinners) rather than an impersonal cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping or systematic cosmological mechanism. No recoverable oldest correspondential substrate can be cleanly extracted from these paragraphs as presented.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue frame: catechumen questions the apostle; recap of what was ‘written down in the books’. Institutional speaker/audience setup and catechumen category mark later editorial framing rather than substrate exposition.
Transitional rubric (‘Then the lord speaks’) introducing two ‘lessons’ (sinner vs catechumen). This is editorial scaffolding, not impersonal teaching.

Direct address and instructional setup (‘listen… I will recount to you… education… given to the catechumens’) signals catechetical/application voice oriented to a church category (catechumens), not a cosmos-internal mapping.
Ethical/disciplinary analogy (children vs servants; rebuke, blows, chains, prison). This is moral-pedagogical rhetoric without cosmological architecture; it functions as pastoral instruction.

Although it contains Light/fire punishment imagery, the paragraph repeatedly anchors the exposition to institutional categories (‘education of the catechumens… the sinners…’) and functions as application of discipline/eschatological warning, not a self-contained cosmological-correspondential mechanism. Too entangled with catechumen/sinner contrast to extract a clear substrate fragment.
Direct beatitude/blessing and ordination language addressed to catechumens (‘Blessed are you… chosen and ordained’) is explicitly ecclesial/pastoral closing material.
